rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters identify a serious systemic problem, direct the responsible official to develop recommendations for the President’s consideration, and anticipate presenting those recommendations to the next session of Congress. The unusually close formulation and shared administrative sequence go beyond generic requests for agency advice. C06 and C23 also commission reviews and recommendations, but their language and intended outputs are less closely aligned with the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Accordingly I would like you to undertake immediately a review of the situation and to develop recommendations which I can consider for presentation to the Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I would appreciate it if you would take the lead in developing for my consideration recommendations which could be made to the next session of Congress on this subject.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel wording combines development of recommendations, presidential consideration, and subsequent submission to Congress.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I informed the Congress of my serious concern over the financial conditions of the railroad retirement and unemployment compensation systems.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is becoming increasingly clear that the current difficulties facing all segments of the transportation industry will require increased leadership and additional actions on the part of the Federal Government.
shared_material.explanation: Each letter opens by identifying difficulties in a transportation-related system as the predicate for executive review and action.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I know you, and the other members of the Board, share my concern in this matter
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Since the Department of Commerce has the statutory authority for the development of a national transportation policy, I am placing the primary responsibility for this task in the Department.
shared_material.explanation: Both address the institutionally responsible official and assign that official the task of producing the requested policy response.
